articles.body: DIMAPUR: At least nine people have died at Tuensang district hospital over the past three days after reportedly consuming spurious liquor, prompting Nagaland director general of police Rupin Sharma to issue an alert advising people to abstain from drinking alcohol.The victims reportedly complained of breathlessness after consuming the suspected adulterated liquor. Their deaths have not yet been officially linked to the alcohol, and the circumstances are under investigation.In a social media post, Sharma said the deaths were suspected to be linked to spurious liquor, possibly a contaminated batch of rum, and described the situation as alarming.He advised people, particularly in Mon, Mokokchung, Tuensang, Longleng, Kiphire, Shamator and Noklak districts, not to consume liquor as a precautionary measure.The DGP said preliminary findings suggested that the victims may have consumed tainted rum.An investigation is under way to trace the source of the suspected contaminated alcohol and identify those responsible.Authorities have also urged the public to remain vigilant and immediately report any suspicious sale or distribution of liquor in their areas.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: ABVP protests Umar Khalid documentary screening at NLSIU
articles.summary: ABVP protests NLSIU’s planned screening of Umar Khalid documentary, calls it propaganda; university says student committee organized it, decision pending.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad on Sunday protested against proposed screening of a documentary on activist Umar Khalid at National Law School of India University on Monday evening.ABVP said that screening amounts “to permitting campus space for propaganda” linked to the jailed activist allegedly part of JNU controversy, Delhi riots and CAA-NRC protests.Filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’ is scheduled for screening from 7am to 8.30am to coincide with Political Prisoners Day. University’s Law and Society Committee has organised the event.The organisation said it had written to NLSIU demanding that the event be called off, but received no response. It has reiterated its demand for immediate cancellation to protect the “institutional integrity”.An NLSIU spokesperson told TOI the screening had been organised by the student committee. As of Sunday evening, the administration had not taken a decision on the matter.An email sent to students said the event marks six years of Khalid’s imprisonment and over six years of Sharjeel Imam’s detention, and would be followed by a discussion on pre-trial detention, bail and dissent.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Kremlin says Modi and Xi offered Putin help to settle Ukraine war
articles.summary: India News: PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered diplomatic support to Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring the Ukraine war to an end, according .
articles.body: PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered diplomatic support to Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring the Ukraine war to an end, according to Russian authorities. “During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution,” said Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, according to a Reuters report. Putin is learned to have welcomed their readiness.Unlike China’s peace blueprint, India has not offered any standalone ceasefire proposal, choosing to play the role of facilitator instead. However, it has gone a step further recently, saying it’s discussing with both sides ideas and suggestions.The past couple of weeks have seen Modi publicly exhorting Putin to stop the “endless” war in a meeting in Bishkek, Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar discussing approaches to end the conflict with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv, and the PM reiterating his peace message to the Russian president in Delhi.Russia: Stand on war aligned with India’s peace callModi and Putin have discussed conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region, which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of seafarers.Briefing journalists before the summit, Peskov said Russia’s position on the war aligned with India’s call for peace. On the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek, Modi had told Putin every day spent in the war pushes humanity back and every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope.China had in 2023 proposed a 12-point plan including proposals like ensuring respect for sovereignty of all nations, ceasing hostilities, resuming peace talks, resolving the humanitarian crisis and keeping nuclear power plants safe.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Sweden opposition holds one-seat advantage over ruling bloc, projection shows as vote counting continues
articles.summary: Europe News: Sweden's national election was too close to call early Monday, with preliminary results giving the left-wing opposition a razor-thin one-seat advantag.
articles.body: Sweden's national election was too close to call early Monday, with preliminary results giving the left-wing opposition a razor-thin one-seat advantage over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right wing coalition and days of uncertainty until the final ballots are counted.Preliminary results showed a very narrow lead for the opposition and former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson's bid to return to office at the head of the left coalition. But Kristersson also said he would explore "possibilities" given the close result.With 92 per cent of the vote counted early Monday, the Swedish Election Authority reported the four opposition parties were heading for 175 seats in the 349-seat parliament to 174 seats for the government alliance.The outcome of the election may not be decided until Wednesday, when local election boards count early votes that did not make it to the polling stations by Election Day. This includes, among others things, overseas votes.Andersson told supporters that "we must wait for the final election result" but added that "right now we are leading ... But we have to wait for the final result."Kristersson has led Sweden since 2022 with a three-party centre-right coalition. It relied on outside support from the Sweden Democrats, an anti-immigration party that has far-right roots but has moved toward the political mainstream, for a parliamentary majority. The Sweden Democrats had been promised Cabinet posts this time if the governing coalition were returned to office."When we have the final result it's a good idea to look at possible combinations," he said early Monday, adding that "there is a very clear non-socialist majority, or non-left leaning economic majority in the Swedish parliament. And I will actually take note of that and at least figure out whether there are any possibilities."Sweden Democrat's leader Jimmie Åkesson said that "we will not know tonight" who will form the next government. The party's support slipped almost 3 per cent from its 2022 result of 20.5 per cent and it fell from second to third place.Exit polls from public broadcaster SVT had initially shown the left-wing parties ahead by several percentage points. The exit polls set off jubilation at the Social Democrats' election gathering but the mood shifted to quiet waiting as the results indicated a closer race.The centre left Social Democrats have led most Swedish governments since World War II. Andersson served as prime minister from 2021 until she lost power at the last election. To return to office she would have to seal a coalition agreement with other parties.There are two major political blocs: one with four parties on the right and another with four parties on the left. So the big question is less about which party wins and more about which side can form a majority. Individual parties need a minimum of 4 per cent of the vote to win parliamentary seats.With broad political consensus in Sweden on several major issues such as support for Ukraine and the country's decision to join NATO, much election discussion focused on the possibility of the anti-immigration hard right entering government. The Sweden Democrats' role was in focus against a background of gains for the populist right in Europe, including the first-place finish by the far-right Alternative for Germany party in a regional election there September 6.The Sweden Democrats were founded in the 1980s by people who had been active in right-wing extremist groups, including neo-Nazis. They toned down their rhetoric and expelled openly racist members under Åkesson, who has led them since 2005 and overseen their growth from what was once a marginal party.More than 8 million people in the nation of about 10.6 million were eligible to vote.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: Heartfelt quotes to share with family and friends

articles.body: There’s a different feeling when Ganpati comes home.The house suddenly gets busier. Someone is arranging flowers, someone is making modaks, children are excited about the decorations and there’s usually a last-minute rush to get everything ready before the aarti.But somewhere in all that noise, there’s also a quiet moment when everyone stands in front of Bappa and prays.That’s what makes Ganesh Chaturthi special for so many families.The festival is also a time to call people you haven't spoken to in a while, send a message to friends and wish loved ones well. And if “Happy Ganesh Chaturthi” feels a little too simple, a heartfelt quote can make the message more personal.Here are some Ganesh Chaturthi quotes and wishes you can share with the people who matter.Ganesh Chaturthi quotes for family“May Bappa keep our family close, our home happy and our hearts full. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi.”“Welcome home, Bappa. Please keep your blessings over our family today and always.”“May there always be laughter in our home, peace in our hearts and Bappa's blessings around us.”“Ganesh Chaturthi is a little more special when the whole family is together. May we always have reasons to celebrate like this.”“Bappa, look after the people we love, keep them healthy and give us more moments together.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi bring our family good health, happiness and the kind of peace that stays long after the festival is over.”“Home feels a little different when Bappa is here. There is more prayer, more laughter and somehow, more warmth.”Ganpati quotes for a fresh startThere’s a reason Lord Ganesha is remembered before a new beginning. So if someone close to you is starting a new job, moving to a new place or simply trying to make a fresh start, Ganesh Chaturthi is a good time to send them a little encouragement.“May Bappa bless your new beginning and give you the confidence to take the first step.”“Whatever comes next, may you have Bappa's blessings and the courage to keep moving forward.”“May Lord Ganesha clear the road ahead and lead you towards better days.”“Starting again isn't always easy. May Bappa give you the strength to do it anyway.”“May every new door that opens bring you closer to the life you've been hoping for.”“Leave the past where it belongs and walk into the new chapter with faith. Bappa is with you.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi be the beginning of something really good in your life.”Short Ganpati quotes for friendsSometimes there's no need to write a long message. A simple wish sent at the right time can mean just as much.“Ganpati Bappa Morya! May your worries be fewer and your happy days many.”“May Bappa keep smiling on you and your family.”“Bappa is home. Let the celebrations begin!”“May Lord Ganesha remove every obstacle in your way.”“Keep the faith and keep going. Bappa has got you.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi bring you good news, good health and plenty of reasons to smile.”“Wishing you a peaceful heart, a happy home and Bappa's blessings always.”“May your life be as sweet as the modaks on your plate this Ganesh Chaturthi.”Ganesh Chaturthi quotes about faithLife doesn't always go according to plan. There are good days, difficult days and plenty of days when we simply don't know what comes next.For many devotees, that's where faith comes in.“Some prayers are said aloud. Some are only whispered in the heart. Bappa hears them all.”“When you don't know what to do next, pause, pray and trust the journey.”“May Bappa give you strength on the days when you feel like giving up.”“Faith doesn't mean that everything will be easy. It means knowing you won't have to face it alone.”“May Lord Ganesha give you the wisdom to make the right choice and the courage to stand by it.”“When life feels uncertain, hold on to faith. The way forward will become clearer.”“May Bappa take away the fear in your heart and replace it with hope.”“Bow your head to the Lord of wisdom and prosperity. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!”Ganpati quotes for happiness and peace“May Bappa bring peace to the things that worry you and happiness to the things that matter.”“May your home be full of laughter and your heart have fewer things to worry about.”“Sometimes the biggest blessing is simply having your loved ones around you. May Bappa keep them close.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi leave you with a lighter heart and a happier home.”“Take a break from the rush, say a prayer, eat a modak and enjoy the people around you.”“May Bappa remind you that the little things in life are often the ones worth holding on to.”“May there be more laughter at home, more peace in your mind and more good days ahead.”Also Read: Happy Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: Best Vinayaka Chaturthi wishes and messages to share with colleagues, employees, friends, and familyGanpati Bappa Morya wishes“Ganpati Bappa Morya! May Bappa's blessings stay with you even after the celebrations end.”“Ganpati Bappa Morya! May every difficult road become a little easier and every new beginning bring hope.”“Bappa, keep our families safe, our hearts peaceful and our homes filled with happiness. Ganpati Bappa Morya!”“May the sound of aarti fill your home, the people you love fill your heart and Bappa's blessings stay with you all year.”“Welcome home, Bappa. Bless us, guide us and give us the strength to handle whatever comes our way.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi bring you the kind of happiness that doesn't need a reason.”“Ganpati Bappa Morya! Here's to fresh starts, family time, good health and happier days.”“May Bappa remove what is holding you back and make room for everything good that is waiting for you.”“Bring Bappa home with faith, celebrate with your loved ones and don't forget to enjoy the little moments along the way.”“Ganpati Bappa Morya! May your home be happy, your heart be peaceful and the year ahead be kind to you.”Ganesh Chaturthi is, of course, about puja and tradition. But it is also about the small things that happen around it. Family members sitting together after the aarti. Children waiting for prasad. Someone sneaking an extra modak from the kitchen. Friends dropping by just to say, “Ganpati Bappa Morya.”Those are the moments people remember.So this Ganesh Chaturthi, send a message that actually sounds like you. It doesn't need to be complicated or overly poetic. Sometimes a simple wish, sent with genuine feeling, is more than enough.“May Bappa stay close, keep your loved ones safe and give you plenty of reasons to smile. articles.title: Super Alvinho volta à escola após viver em abrigo no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Após repercussão, família de menino com altas habilidades conseguiu juntar dinheiro com doações e com a venda de livros dele.
articles.summary: Super Alvinho, menino com altas habilidades, retoma os estudos após viver em abrigo no Rio e receber apoio em uma corrente de solidariedade.
articles.body:
Álvaro de Melo, de 10 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo Pessoal

O menino conhecido como Super Alvinho, que tem altas habilidades e estava vivendo em um abrigo do Grajaú , no Rio, deve voltar à escola nesta segunda-feira (14).

Álvaro Siqueira de Melo tem 10 anos e já desenvolveu um aplicativo para Harvard contando as dificuldades de um menino negro na comunidade.

Ele e a mãe, Priscila de Melo, estavam vivendo em um abrigo por enfrentarem dificuldades financeiras durante um tratamento da mãe contra tuberculose, mas neste domingo (13) conseguiram retornar para Cabo Frio, onde moram atualmente por ele ter ganhado uma bolsa de estudos em uma escola particular.

No tempo em que ele ficou no abrigo, ele não pôde frequentar o colégio e Priscila encontrou dificuldades para conseguir concluir o mestrado , tendo estudado de um coworking de um shopping.

Com a repercussão do caso depois de uma matéria do jornal O Globo, uma corrente de solidariedade, que incluiu um pedido de doações do apresentador Luciano Huck, se formou e a família conseguiu R$ 203 mil em doações e com venda de livros dele.

A família agora quer comprar um imóvel no Rio, mas Alvinho pretende concluir os estudos em Cabo Frio antes.

"Como faltam 3 meses para encerrar o ano letivo, e o Álvaro quer muito concluir este ano junto com a turminha dele, retornamos para Cabo Frio para ele fechar este ciclo e em dezembro pretendemos retornar ao Rio, já pra morar na nossa casa própria e iniciar o ano em uma das escolas no Rio que entraram em contato para oferecer bolsa de estudos integral. Também estamos visitando para ele fazer a melhor escolha. Tem surgido propostas de trabalho também e em breve estarei trabalhando."

Eles embarcaram neste domingo (13) na Rodoviária do Rio para Cabo Frio, onde vão continuar morando até dezembro para depois retornar ao Rio.

“Oi, pessoal, eu estou aqui na Rodoviária e amanhã cedo eu já volto para a escola. Eu estou muito feliz que amanhã já vou rever meus colegas”, declarou.

Super Alvinho e a mãe Priscila de Melo — Foto: Reprodução

Na capital, outras escolas particulares já ofereceram bolsas de estudo ao menino, que ele está avaliando.

“Ele está muito feliz, está conhecendo cada escola que ofereceu a bolsa de estudo”, afirmou a mãe.

articles.title: Comunidade rural de Rio da Serra, em Montes Claros, ganha ponte de concreto | G1
articles.standfirst: População celebra o novo acesso.
articles.summary: População celebra o novo acesso.
articles.body:
O Município de Montes Claros, por meio da Secretaria de Agricultura, Pecuária e Desenvolvimento Rural, segue com o trabalho de construção e recuperação de pontes em toda a zona rural da cidade. Além disso, tem intensificado as reformas das estradas rurais, que beneficiam diariamente cerca de 20 mil moradores, permitindo o escoamento da produção, o transporte escolar e a movimentação das equipes da Estratégia de Saúde da Família (ESF).

Recentemente, o Município finalizou uma nova ponte na comunidade de Rio da Serra. Feita inteiramente de concreto, a ponte trará benefícios não apenas para os moradores da comunidade, mas para toda a região do entorno.

O vaqueiro João Edmilson Ferreira Lopes afirma estar “muito grato por esse benefício tão esperado por nós aqui do Rio da Serra. A construção desta ponte era um sonho que esperávamos há mais de 20 anos".

articles.title: Brasileira desaparecida em Veneza havia se casado há 3 meses e queria trabalhar com pesca com o marido | G1
articles.standfirst: Gabriela Elorriaga sumiu após embarcação do casal colidir com táxi aquático na Itália. Italiano teve morte confirmada e buscas continuam na lagoa de Veneza.
articles.summary: Gabriela Elorriaga sumiu após embarcação do casal colidir com táxi aquático na Itália. Italiano teve morte confirmada e buscas continuam na lagoa de Veneza.
articles.body:
O italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, e a brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26, em Veneza, na Itália. — Foto: Redes sociais

Desaparecida após uma colisão entre embarcações em Veneza , na Itália, a brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26 anos, se casou há três meses com o italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, e se preparava para trabalhar com pesca ao lado do marido.

"Ela estava conseguindo a vida lá, vivendo, e estava vivendo feliz", diz Gisele Elorriaga, mãe da jovem.

Natural de Ribeirão Preto (SP), a jovem desapareceu na Itália após a lancha em que o casal estava colidir com um táxi aquático e afundar.

Até a última atualização desta notícia, ela não tinha sido localizada pelas autoridades italianas. O Itamaraty acompanha o caso.

O acidente aconteceu na madrugada de sábado (12) no Canal de Tessera, localizado na Lagoa de Veneza , trecho que realiza a ligação com o aeroporto local. A embarcação ocupada pelo casal acabou afundando após ser atingida pelo táxi aquático.

O marido da brasileira, Sean Michieli, chegou a ser resgatado em estado grave com traumatismo craniano e múltiplos ferimentos, mas teve a morte cerebral confirmada no hospital. Gabriela, no entanto, caiu na água e permaneceu desaparecida.

Com mais de 24 horas de operações, mergulhadores dos bombeiros, policiais e equipes de resgate italianas realizam varreduras na área.

Até então, os agentes haviam localizado a embarcação submersa e alguns objetos pessoais da brasileira.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) informou que, por meio do Consulado-Geral em Milão, acompanha o caso e presta assistência em contato direto com as autoridades locais e os familiares.

Gabriela havia se mudado para a Itália há cerca de dois anos e oficializou o casamento com Sean em junho deste ano.

Para exercer a atividade profissional ao lado do companheiro, a jovem estava providenciando as documentações necessárias e dava andamento ao processo para tirar a licença exigida para trabalhar com pesca.

De acordo com a família, navegar por aquela área, principalmente próximo à Ilha de Burano, fazia parte da rotina do casal.

"Eles conheciam, [tinham] costume, eles atravessam de um lado para o outro, até para a localização que lá é tudo dentro do barco mesmo", afirma Gisele.

No Brasil, a mãe da jovem declarou, no domingo, que ainda tinha esperanças de encontrar a filha com vida. "Eu só quero minha filha de volta com vida, mais nada."

Gabriela e Sean estavam casados há três meses; os dois se envolveram em acidente de barco no canal de Veneza. — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.title: UK Weather: Turning cooler, wetter and windier this week
articles.summary: A stronger jet stream will bring a distinctly autumnal look to our weather this week, but is there a September heatwave on the horizon later this month?
articles.body:
Changeable autumnal conditions are set to continue through this coming week, with spells of wetter and windier weather developing at times.

Monday will bring a short-lived burst of warmth and sunshine before temperatures drop to levels more typical for September later in the week.

A strengthening jet stream will bring deeper, low-pressure systems as the week goes on, with the potential for minor disruption towards next weekend.

Higher pressure looks set to build again for the end of the month, but prospects of a late-September heatwave remain uncertain.

Strengthening jet stream to bring windier weather

The jet stream is a ribbon of fast-moving air high in the atmosphere, around six miles above our heads, and its shape, speed and position help dictate what type of weather we experience.

During the start to the week, the jet stream will be relatively weak and loop to the north of the UK, allowing higher pressure to develop and a warm south-westerly airflow to take hold.

Later, the jet stream will take on a more southerly path, flowing faster and straighter towards our shores. This will mean lower pressure will form, bringing rain and brisk winds at times, and temperatures will drop.

Monday will be the warmest day of the week, with the air coming in from a south-westerly direction.

Many areas will stay fairly cloudy, with some rain around coasts and hills in the west. Despite this it will feel warm and rather humid, with temperatures climbing above 20C in many places.

Where the sun does break through, in central and southern parts of England, temperatures could reach as high as 26C.

By Thursday the winds will turn more westerly or north-westerly, bringing a fresher air mass and a cooler feel to the weather. Temperatures by this stage will reach around 14 to 16C in Scotland and Northern Ireland, and 17 to 20C in England and Wales.

Will we see September out with a heatwave?

Forecasts are showing that areas of high pressure should have more influence on the weather for the last week of September. This may mean longer dry interludes and the chance of returning to above-average daytime temperatures, but the degree of temperature rise will depend on the positioning the high pressure relative to the UK.

While long-range forecasting is fraught with uncertainty and details are subject to change, there is currently nothing to indicate that a heatwave is on the cards.

Indeed, as autumn advances and the nights become longer, high pressure overhead could lead to some rather chilly mornings.

You can keep an eye on the temperatures where you are by checking BBC Weather online and the app .

articles.body: Braden “Clavicular” is making a strong claim about his place in internet culture after Ludwig included him among his five picks for Streamer of the Year 2026. The recognition has sparked debate over just how far Clavicular’s influence reaches beyond livestreaming. Rather than dismissing the attention, the streamer responded with confidence while also admitting that he has not been streaming as often lately.Clavicular reacts to Ludwig’s Streamer of the Year pickLudwig recently revealed the creators he would nominate for the 2026 Streamer of the Year award. His list included Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed, Stable Ronaldo, Jynxzi and Clavicular.Clavicular’s inclusion stood out because Ludwig knew it could divide viewers. Still, he argued that the streamer’s impact has been difficult to ignore. In his view, Clavicular may have influenced online culture more than anyone else on the list.Ludwig said:"Dude, if I’m being super transparent, if I were to come up with five people to nominate for Streamer of the Year, I would do Kai Cenat, I would do IShowSpeed, I would do Ron, I would do Jynxzi, and I would probably do Clavicular. And that might ruffle some feathers, but I do think he’s probably had the largest impact, maybe, of the list from the streaming space on culture."The comment quickly gained traction after a clip from Ludwig’s stream circulated online. Clavicular then reposted the clip and offered his own assessment of his influence."Easily the biggest impact on culture, but I don't stream enough recently."That response says plenty about how Clavicular views his current position. He believes his cultural reach remains significant even without maintaining a heavy streaming schedule.The discussion also highlights how the definition of a successful streamer has changed. A creator does not necessarily need to be live every day to remain part of the wider online conversation. Viral moments, trends and crossover appeal can keep a personality in front of audiences long after a particular stream ends.Clavicular says he wants a bigger impactClavicular has also suggested that his ambitions now stretch beyond simply building a successful streaming career. In a recent post, he reflected on his purpose and said he wants to use his platform for something more meaningful."For the first time in a while, I've really been contemplating my purpose on this earth. I know I'm on a divine path in some way; I know I'm more than a streamer who hits mogs at clubs. Operating at a higher level to have a real impact."The statement offers another side of Clavicular’s public persona. His focus appears to be shifting from online visibility toward the kind of influence he believes can last beyond individual streams.Whether that translates into a major award recognition remains to be seen. The Streamer Awards will ultimately decide the winners, but Ludwig’s nomination has already placed Clavicular firmly in the conversation.For now, the biggest takeaway is simple. articles.title: Quote of the day by Sadhguru: "Spirituality is not about becoming special, it is about becoming one with everything."; What does the yogi advise on understanding the real meaning of spirituality
articles.summary: Sadhguru is a yogi, mystic, and author. He often talks about associating spirituality with the essence of a positive perspective in daily life through.
articles.body: Sadhguru is a yogi, mystic, and author. He often talks about associating spirituality with the essence of a positive perspective in daily life through his discourses, teachings, and social media posts. Apart from this, he was awarded the Padma Vibhushan, the country's second-highest civilian award, for his contribution to spirituality.He once discussed the idea of success, which often looks like relentless striving, but this process can become exhausting.We live in a world obsessed with standing out, and from a young age, most of us are taught that success means becoming someone who has name and fame, someone whose name people remember, whose face gets recognised, whose life looks different from everyone else's. This run for specialness has quietly become the default definition of a meaningful life.But somewhere along the way, this constant chasing of success to be exceptional starts to feel exhausting. It creates comparison, insecurity, and a constant sense of dissatisfaction that we're never quite enough. Ironically, the more we try to separate ourselves from others to feel special, the more disconnected and alone we tend to feel.Similarly, Sadhguru also talks about the idea of spirituality by associating it with success, and how we see it as becoming someone specialQuote of the daySpirituality is not about becoming special, it is about becoming one with everythingWhat does the quote mean?While most of us grow up thinking that growth means becoming more exceptional, with a better version of ourselves compared to others, someone with a unique identity, special achievements, an outstanding "brand." Even spirituality, ironically, often gets treated the same way. Sadhguru beautifully explains how people chase spiritual experiences hoping to feel enlightened, superior, or somehow above the ordinary chaos of life. But his idea is different.Sadhguru suggests that real spirituality isn't about elevation; it's about dissolution. Not dissolving in a sad or negative sense, but dissolving the walls we've built between "me" and "everything else."So much of our pain comes from feeling separate, like we're on our own with our problems, always competing with others, always guarding who we are, always defending our ego.But when that feeling of separateness starts to fade, even just a bit, life gets lighter. You no longer feel the need to prove you're special, because you no longer feel like some lonely little island trying to matter in a big, uncaring world. Instead, you start to feel connected to people, to nature, to everything around you.This isn't just poetic language. It explains something many contemplative traditions have talked of for centuries: that our natural state isn't isolation, but it's connection: becoming one.Why does this matter today?While our digitally driven world has made us all ‘connected’ online, in reality people are hardly able to make time for each other. People are just busy looking perfect on social media but do not try to perfect their relationships in real life.Similarly, Sadhguru is not asking us to stop striving or stop growing. It's asking us to loosen our grip on the need to be exceptional, and instead notice our natural connection to people, nature, and life around us. Something as simple as spending time outdoors, listening with all attention and empathy to another person without judgment, or sitting silently without trying to "achieve" anything can bring a taste of this oneness.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Russia's Stalin-admiring provincial leader waging an ultra-conservative crusade
articles.summary: An ex-kickboxer preaching Orthodox traditions who has effectively banned abortion and declared war on alcohol: ultra-conservative governor Georgy Filimonov i...
articles.body:
An ex-kickboxer preaching Orthodox traditions who has effectively banned abortion and declared war on alcohol: ultra-conservative governor Georgy Filimonov is the face of Vladimir Putin's rule in Russia's Vologda region.

Accused of authoritarianism and trampling women's rights, Filimonov will represent the ruling United Russia party in this month's tightly-controlled parliamentary elections.

Some 450 kilometres (280 miles) north-west of Moscow, the 45-year-old nationalistic regional leader has built up a reputation for his outspoken views and made national headlines.

In the historic city of Vologda, 31-year-old worker Artyom told AFP a joke was circulating in the neighbouring Yaroslavl region: "When people from Vologda come to us, it's for alcohol, petrol or to get an abortion."

Filimonov has run the region since 2023, one of the social conservative officials promoted by the Kremlin during its more than four-year war in Ukraine.

The 46-year-old bespectacled former kickboxing champion, with the build of a weightlifter, speaks Spanish and French and likes mixing with intellectuals.

Russia, Filimonov said in June during a discussion with far-right ideologue Alexander Dugin, faces the double threat of "depopulation" and "alcohol genocide... orchestrated by our former foreign partners".

For Russia's decades-long struggle with high levels of alcohol-related deaths, he blamed the West, which Moscow says is de-facto at war with Russia.

His rhetoric echoes Putin, who lambasts the "decadent" West and warns of its "deleterious" influence on Russia -- a "besieged" fortress where birth rates are at their lowest in 200 years.

Filimonov hopes his hardline arguments will be enough to convince the region's one million or so residents to join his conservative crusade.

In his three years managing the region, to the alarm of women's rights groups, he has severely restricted abortion access.

Human Rights Watch calls it a "de-facto ban".

"There is no decree" banning abortion in Vologda, Irina Fainman, of the independent Emergency Contraceptive Stockpile Fund, told AFP.

"It is being carried out by non-legislative means and through some sort of illegal measures," Fainman added.

"The governor's administration is putting pressure on the region's healthcare facilities," she said, calling the measures "authoritarian and regressive".

While authorities say the ban is meant to improve birthrates, in reality it "only leads to abortion tourism", Fainman said, with women travelling to other regions.

Filimonov, however, has remained defiant, declaring at the start of the year that Vologda had "overcome depopulation".

Those most directly affected by his policies, however, find them hard to accept.

Oksana -- whose name has been changed -- said she believed abortion should be a "personal matter".

Filimonov refused AFP's request for an interview.

The hardline governor has made fighting alcoholism the other pillar of his agenda.

Unlike his campaign on abortion, the anti-alcohol drive is regulated by local law, with a ban on shops selling alcoholic drinks outside a two-hour window of 12:00-14:00 on weekdays.

AFP saw Nadezhda, 52, filling her shopping basket with bottles of "Chateau Rouge" -- a Russian wine -- in a supermarket in Vologda's city centre.

The result? "We buy tonnes of bottles in a single go."

Some have questioned whether Filimonov's extravagant measures are a show.

But British historian James Pearce, who lives in Russia and edited a contribution by the governor to an anthology, said Filimonov "actually believes the things he says."

"It is not an act... He is a conservative person," he told AFP.

In 2024, Filimonov erected a statue of Joseph Stalin in Vologda, heralding the Soviet dictator -- responsible for widespread mass-killings and atrocities during his rule -- as an "extraordinary personality".

While Filimonov's style has worried even Putin supporters, the Kremlin has voiced no public objections.

Moscow followed Vologda last year by also inaugurating a statue of Stalin in the capital's metro.

In this month's parliamentary elections, Filimonov -- like other Kremlin-backed officials -- is guaranteed an easy victory, in the absence of any meaningful opposition.

He is unlikely, however, to relinquish his control of Vologda for a seat in the State Duma -- a popular practice known as the "locomotive", when well-known candidates top the ballot paper, only to step aside in favour of a less famous colleague.

articles.body: A Maryland couple was arrested after the death of their 2-month-old daughter who suffered head injuries, with the father allegedly telling police the girl's injuries were caused by "Satan slamming a door on the child," according to charging documents and prosecutors. A later examination revealed what charging documents describe as "significant head and brain trauma" and "multiple skull fractures" that were not noticed during the initial examination, charging documents state, according to CBS Baltimore. IDAHO MOM WHO CLAIMED VACCINES KILLED HER TWIN BABIES CHARGED WITH MURDERING HER KIDS The girl's father allegedly claimed to police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." The mother said her 2-year-old son often jumps on the bed, which caused the baby to fall onto the floor, a prosecutor said at a court hearing on Friday, according to the outlet. The prosecutor argued that the extent of the girl's injuries could not have been caused by a single fall from the bed. articles.title: Shot down over Iran, hunted for 50 hours: How US fighter survived behind enemy lines
articles.summary: US News: A US Air Force officer revealed how he survived for nearly 50 hours in Iran after his F-15E fighter jet was shot down during a strike mission in April.
articles.body: A US Air Force officer revealed how he survived for nearly 50 hours in Iran after his F-15E fighter jet was shot down during a strike mission in April. He shared that more than 90 American service members were eventually deployed in one of the most complex US military rescue operations in recent history.The officer, a weapons-systems officer identified by his mission call sign as “Dude 44 Bravo”, was rescued on Easter Sunday after spending two days injured and hiding in Iran’s mountainous desert, while Iranian forces searched for him. He had suffered a broken back, arm and shoulder after falling at an estimated 70-100 mph when the missile damaged his parachute.The details were revealed in Bravo’s first public account of the incident in an interview with CBS News’ 60 Minutes.US launches massive operation to find BravoThe rescue operation involved hundreds of personnel in the air and thousands more supporting the mission, according to Adm Brad Cooper, the US central command commander. More than 90 US service members were on the ground in Iran, marking the first deployment of US ground troops there in 46 years, Cooper said.The US military also used bombers and drones to strike IRGC forces near Bravo’s hiding place before sending in the final rescue team. The CIA played a key role by using a deception campaign to confuse Iranian forces and employing classified technology to locate the downed officer.Bravo said he was badly injured but continued moving after landing about five miles from his pilot, identified as “Alpha”.“I had injuries, but we all train to adapt and overcome the things that we're faced with,” he said. “I moved as quickly as I could, despite the injuries, away from the place that I landed.”He eventually climbed to a 7,000-foot ridgeline, where he remained hidden from Iranian forces.Iranian forces came close to finding himUS military officials said Iranian ground forces were actively searching for the two airmen after their F-15E went down.“There was clear intent out of the Iranian ground force to come find those two guys,” Gen Dan Caine, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, said.Alpha was rescued about six hours after the US learnt of the crash in a risky daytime operation. The rescue helicopters came under fire, according to US defence secretary Pete Hegseth.“It was a gun fight all the way in and all the way out,” Hegseth said. “But they got Alpha back.”Bravo, however, could not be located during that operation and had to spend another day alone in the mountains with almost no food or water.He eventually managed to send a message to the US.“When I got to the moment where I could review and think about all that I'd gone through, I sent, 'God is good,' as a recognition of all that he had brought me through,” Bravo said.F-15E was shot down during Iran strikeThe F-15E, a two-seat fighter valued at about $30 million, was brought down by an Iranian shoulder-fired missile on April 2 during a US strike mission near Isfahan.The mission targeted industrial facilities linked to Iran’s drone and missile programme, according to Cooper. The area was also close to locations where Iran had stored much of its highly enriched nuclear material.“When I looked up and saw no parachute, that was the most terrifying thing I've ever seen,” Bravo said.“So I paused, right then, and I prayed, 'Lord, your will be done. But if I'm getting through this, I need help.'”The damaged aircraft forced both crew members to eject. Alpha was rescued first and has since returned to flying duties.The final rescue force reached Bravo at dawn on Easter Sunday using small “Little Bird” helicopters after landing rescue aircraft on a makeshift desert airstrip.“Let's go,” Bravo said he told his rescuers when they reached him.The rescue operation itself then ran into another crisis. The landing gear of two rescue aircraft became stuck in the desert sand, leaving more than 90 US personnel stranded. The US eventually destroyed the two aircraft and the Little Bird helicopters to prevent their technology from falling into Iranian hands.Bravo described his survival as a “modern-day miracle” and said the mission demonstrated the US commitment to recovering its personnel.“I believe that it's a testament to God's provision in my life to bring me through that moment in a way that didn't prevent injuries, but prevented any catastrophic injuries that would have affected my ability to survive,” he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. The candidates would be announced on Sept 15, said CPI state secretary M Veerapandian.The decision was taken at state committee meetings of the two parties in Trichy and Chennai. Their support for the TVK-led govt, however, would continue, the leaders said.Though CPI and CPM have been critical of TVK, the decision has come as a surprise for many because the Left would have to campaign against the govt they support, said political watchers.Defending the decision, Shanmugam said support for the govt does not mean CPM should not adopt a position to strengthen the organisation. He said contesting the byelections did not mean that CPM was threatening the stability of TVK govt.“Nor does it mean that we support DMK. Left parties are not part of any of the three alliances. This is not a general election or an election to change govt,” he said.Veerapandian echoed the same. The Left leaders said the bypolls would be used to strengthen their presence in the assembly and amplify the voice of workers and ordinary people.“There was a strong sentiment in our executive committee meeting for this position,” he said. Shanmugam took an indirect dig at TVK for accommodating the resigned AIADMK MLAs, which has resulted in the bypoll.“We have said it was wrong for two MLAs — who won on the AIADMK symbol in the assembly election — to resign and join TVK, and that horse-trading was involved,” he said.He said their campaign would focus on TVK govt’s performance and the issues on which the Left had differed with it.“We have expressed our differences of opinion on many occasions, including the budget. We have urged ministers on what laws should be passed and not passed. A few were accepted, but many were not. We have urged that the legislative assembly should serve as a democratic forum for discussing people’s issues. All this will find focus in the campaign,” he said.Veerapandian said drug abuse, law and order problems and lack of infrastructure would be raised in their campaignThe decision is seen as an extension of the Left’s stand of “supporting the govt to prevent a BJP intrusion”. articles.body: There is a special warmth in the days leading up to Ganesh Chaturthi. Homes begin to come alive with flowers and decorations, idols of Lord Ganesha are brought home with devotion, and the familiar sound of prayers and aartis slowly becomes part of the festive atmosphere. For devotees, welcoming Bappa is not only a celebration but also a time to seek his blessings for wisdom, happiness, peace and the strength to overcome obstacles.This year, Ganesh Chaturthi will be celebrated on Monday, September 14, 2026. The festival will bring families and communities together in prayer and celebration, with beautifully decorated pandals, traditional rituals, aartis and, of course, festive delicacies such as modaks.And as loved ones come together to celebrate, wishes become a simple way of sharing the spirit of the festival with those who may not be close by. Whether you are sending a message to your family, a friend, a colleague or your team at work, the right words can make the greeting feel a little more personal.Here are some heartfelt Ganesh Chaturthi wishes and messages you can share with your loved ones this year.For family - because these are the people who'll actually read the whole message“Ganpati Bappa is home again, and so is that lovely madness of modaks, aarti timings, and everyone squeezing into the living room for darshan. Wishing our family a Ganesh Chaturthi filled with laughter, good food, and Bappa's blessings all year round.”“No matter how far we are, Bappa's arrival always brings us back to the same feeling - home. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi to the people who make every festival feel complete.”“This year, may Ganpati Bappa remove every obstacle standing between you and your peace of mind -and maybe also help you find parking near the pandal. Happy Vinayaka Chaturthi!”“Some things never change - the smell of fresh modaks, and mom reminding everyone to wake up early for the puja. Wouldn't want it any other way. Ganpati Bappa Morya!”For friends - a little cheeky, a little heartfelt“May Bappa bless you with everything you're manifesting - and also give you the willpower to stop at just three modaks. (We both know that's not happening.) Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!”“Here's to another year of Bappa watching over our chaos, our plans that never work out, and our questionable life choices. Ganpati Bappa Morya, my friend!”“You, me, loud dhol beats, and way too many modaks - that's basically the plan for the next ten days. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!”“Wishing you a Ganesh Chaturthi as sorted as you pretend your life is on Instagram. Jokes aside, may Bappa bring you genuine peace and good vibes this season.”For colleagues - warm but not awkwardly personal“Wishing you and your family a joyful Ganesh Chaturthi. May this festive season bring fresh energy, good health, and a well-deserved break from back-to-back meetings.”“As Bappa settles in for the next ten days, hope you get to enjoy some well-deserved festive downtime with your loved ones. Happy Vinayaka Chaturthi!”“Sending warm Ganesh Chaturthi wishes your way. Here's hoping this festival brings a little extra calm before the next big deadline sneaks up on us.”“May Lord Ganesha's blessings guide us through the rest of the year with clarity, patience, and hopefully a lot fewer last-minute client calls. Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!”“Ganesh Chaturthi reminds us to embrace new journeys with faith and courage—wishing you the best in all your endeavors.”For employees - something a manager or HR team can actually aend without it sounding like circular“On behalf of the entire team, wishing everyone a very Happy Ganesh Chaturthi. Thank you for your hard work this year - take this time to recharge, celebrate, and enjoy the festival with your families.”“As we welcome Ganpati Bappa, we also want to take a moment to appreciate the effort each one of you brings to work every single day. Wishing you a festival filled with joy and much-needed rest.”“May this Ganesh Chaturthi bring new beginnings, renewed energy, and a lot of positivity as we head into the last quarter of the year together. Happy celebrations to you and your family!”For your WhatsApp status or Instagram caption“Ganpati Bappa Morya!”“New idol, same old excitement. Bappa's home.”“Ten days of devotion, dhol, and definitely too many modaks.”“May Ganpati remove every obstacle you didn't even know you had.”A quick note before you hit sendIf you're sending these to a group chat, a little personalisation goes a long way - swap in a name, add an inside joke, or just tweak the tone depending on who's reading it. A message to your building's WhatsApp group probably needs a different energy than the one you send your best friend from college.Whatever way you choose to celebrate this year - a grand pandal visit, a quiet puja at home, or simply calling up your parents because you can't make it back this time - may this Ganesh Chaturthi bring exactly the kind of peace, joy, and good fortune Bappa is known for.Ganpati Bappa Morya, Mangal Murti Morya!Thumb image: Canva (for representative purposes only)Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: World’s biggest bank to investment banking candidates: We want to know how you use AI to …
articles.summary: Tech News News: ​UBS is asking prospective junior investment bankers to prove that they know how to use artificial intelligence (AI). With this move, one of the world.
articles.body: ​UBS is asking prospective junior investment bankers to prove that they know how to use artificial intelligence (AI). With this move, one of the world’s largest private banks is making AI proficiency part of its hiring process for graduates and interns joining its global banking and markets divisions in 2027. The Swiss bank is among the first large financial institutions to explicitly require AI literacy for junior banking candidates.​A Financial Times report cited people familiar with the matter, who said the bank wants candidates to show how they can use AI to “improve outcomes and efficiency”. The requirement will sit alongside more traditional criteria, including being on track to obtain a 2.1 undergraduate degree, and AI “fluency” questions will be added to recruitment interviews for graduate trainees and interns.​Why UBS is testing AI skills in junior bankers​The updated interview questions will focus on how candidates have used AI, not whether they know about the technology. The requirement is part of a wider shift in the skills banks are looking for as they deploy AI tools to tasks traditionally done by junior staff.​This includes tasks such as financial analysis, research and preparing presentations for clients. UBS said the AI requirement would also apply to other newly advertised roles across the firm, suggesting the focus on AI capabilities is not limited to its graduate and internship programmes.​UBS said: “We continuously review our recruitment criteria to ensure they reflect the skills we need. As AI is fundamentally reshaping financial services, AI capabilities and experiences have become an important aspect of future professional success and are as such relevant recruiting criteria.”​How UBS is using AI internally​Apart from hiring, UBS has also been experimenting with AI in its internal operations. The bank has created analyst avatars that can deliver video presentations to clients, freeing staff to focus on other tasks.UBS said: “AI literacy complements, rather than replaces, the academic, analytical and interpersonal skills that remain core to our approach to hiring talent.”​Other banks are also looking for AI users​UBS is not the only bank adding AI skills to its recruitment criteria. Spain's Santander has explicitly sought “advanced AI users” for some graduate programmes in its corporate and investment bank, according to company filings.This is happening as financial institutions use AI to automate routine processes to reduce the risk of job losses, an issue being flagged across the industry. In recent predictions made by Morgan Stanley analysts, over 200,000 jobs in the European banking sector are set to become redundant within the next five years.​How banks face a training challenge​Some banking executives have warned that greater reliance on AI should not come at the expense of basic financial and banking knowledge. Conor Hillery, JPMorgan Chase’s co-head for Europe, Middle East and Africa, said at the FT’s global banking summit last year that lenders needed to be “very careful” that employees did not “lose an understanding of the basics and fundamentals”.​JPMorgan was seeking to strike a balance between using AI to streamline simple processes and educating young employees on banking basics through core skills, Hillery opined. If technology took over responsibilities usually given to new recruits, they would have no opportunity to learn the basics through practical work.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.summary: Tech News News: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for targeting Citadel CEO Ken Griffin in a viral Tax Day video promoting p.
articles.body: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for targeting Citadel CEO Ken Griffin in a viral Tax Day video promoting proposed pied-à-terre tax. Speaking with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bezos said: “When you don’t know how to solve a problem, create a villain, blame them. But it won’t solve the problem. The only thing that will solve the problem is skill.” Griffin had called the video “creepy” and threatened to cancel a $6 billion Midtown development project, prompting mediation by Governor Kathy Hochul.Jeff Bezos is supporting the tax but rejecting the targetingBezos, who owns a residence in New York City and would himself be subject to the proposed tax, did not oppose the policy itself. He called a pied-à-terre tax “a fine thing for New York to do,” likening it to hotel taxes that fall on out-of-towners. But he drew a clear line against Mamdani’s tactic of filming outside Griffin’s $238 million penthouse. “Ken Griffin isn’t a villain. He hasn’t hurt anybody. He’s not hurting New York. In fact, quite the opposite,” Bezos said.Jeff Bezos redirects the argumentWhile distancing himself from the personal feud, Bezos shifted the conversation toward government inefficiency. “Any corporate CEO, CFO worth their salt—an Amazon CFO could find 3% in the federal budget on a Tuesday afternoon. There is so much waste in government spending,” he argued, suggesting fiscal discipline rather than higher taxes is the real solution.Jeff Bezos criticised Zohran Mamdani’s economic policiesThis is not the first time that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has criticised New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Recently, Bezos criticised New York City’s public school spending and Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s economic policies. He argued that increased funding alone does not solve the underlying issues. During an interview on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Bezos compared the city’s education system with Amazon’s operations, saying inefficiencies in public administration would not be tolerated in business. “If we ran Amazon the way New York City runs their school system, your packages would take six weeks to arrive. We’d have to charge you a $100 delivery fee. And then when the package did finally arrive, it’d have the wrong item in it anyway,” Bezos told CNBC.He followed up by clashing with Zohran Mamdani over billionaire taxes, arguing that raising taxes on the wealthy would not materially improve life for working-class residents. Mamdani countered: “I know a few teachers in Queens who would beg to differ.”Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Turkish authorities launch anti-LGBTQ raids, detaining dozens
articles.summary: Turkish police raid LGBTQ groups across major cities, detaining at least 63 in a major crackdown.
articles.body:
Turkish police have detained dozens of people after conducting nationwide raids targeting LGBTQ organisations.

Police swooped on gay bars, offices and homes of activists in major cities including Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and Mersin on Sunday, escalating Turkiye’s decade-long hostility towards LGBTQ groups.

State news agency Anadolu quoted prosecutors in Ankara, Istanbul and Izmir as saying that at least 63 people were detained, the AFP news agency reported.

Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said in a social media post on Sunday that prosecutors had launched an investigation into 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses to “protect children, the institution of the family, and public order”.

Turkish authorities targeted current and former members of multiple LGBTQ rights and HIV awareness groups. The organisations’ websites were blocked days before the police raids.

Gurlek said the “My Family is Safe” operations on Sunday aligned with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s 10-year “Decade of Family and Population” executive order, which aims to combat Turkiye’s falling birthrate.

“As per the duty to protect families and children given to the state by the constitution, no criminal organization, abuse network or illegal activity which targets children, youths or families will be tolerated!” Gurlek wrote on X.

LGBTQ rights organisation Kaos GL, whose offices were searched and activists taken into custody, said that “nearly 50 defenders of the rights of LGBTQ people … have been taken into custody or are subject to legal proceedings involving interrogations or detentions”.

Judicial authorities in Turkiye’s capital, Ankara, accused Kaos GL of publishing “posts containing obscenity” online and said that the content was accessible to children, according to the rights group.

Rights activists accused the Turkish government of hardening its rhetoric and restrictions against Turkiye’s LGBTQ community in recent years.

“The real name of this operation is not ‘My Family is Safe’; it is state-led discrimination, politics of fear and the dismantling of civil society,” the Turkish Human Rights Association said on X.

The European Parliament’s rapporteur on Turkiye, Nacho Sanchez Amor, condemned the detentions as “a shocking escalation in the repression” in the country.

The governing AK Party banned Istanbul Pride in 2015. Any attempted gatherings since then have been violently dispersed by authorities.

articles.title: Russia offers Rs 16 lakh per foreign soldier for Ukraine war: Report
articles.summary: Europe News: Russia’s Irkutsk region has sharply increased financial incentives for recruiting foreign nationals into the country’s military, offering up to 1.5 mi.
articles.body: Russia’s Irkutsk region has sharply increased financial incentives for recruiting foreign nationals into the country’s military, offering up to 1.5 million rubles (around Rs 16 lakh) for each foreign citizen or stateless person recruited to fight in the war against Ukraine.According to The Kyiv Independent, which cited independent Russian outlet Vyorstka, the new payment was established in a decree signed earlier this week by Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev. The payment is reportedly the highest reward offered by any Russian region for recruiting foreign nationals into the military.Irkutsk has offered financial incentives for recruiting contract soldiers since at least April. Previously, recruiters could receive up to 400,000 rubles (around $4,700). The latest increase means the maximum payment for recruiting a foreign national has risen almost fourfold in seven months, Vyorstka reported.The new decree also creates a separate category for foreign nationals and stateless people for the first time. Meanwhile, the payment for recruiting Russian citizens who are registered outside Irkutsk Oblast has been doubled from 400,000 rubles to 800,000 rubles (around $9,500).Russia turns to foreign recruitsThe increase in Irkutsk comes as Russian regions step up recruitment incentives amid Moscow's continuing need for manpower in its war against Ukraine.Other regions have also raised payments for those helping recruit soldiers. Smolensk Oblast increased its recruiter payment from 115,000 rubles (around $1,300) to 1 million rubles (around $11,900), while Ryazan Oblast has raised some recruitment payments to 805,000 rubles (around $9,500).The growing incentives also come amid increasing evidence that Russia has sought to bolster its military ranks with foreign nationals, particularly people from lower-income countries.The recruitment drive comes as fighting between Russia and Ukraine continues to intensify. Russia has stepped up its air campaign against Ukraine in recent weeks, with ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones being used in attacks across the country. Ukrainian officials have also reported Russian strikes near the border with Poland.At the same time, Ukraine has continued targeting Russian oil and industrial infrastructure with long-range strikes. US President Donald Trump has called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacks on Russian diesel facilities, saying they were contributing to a global fuel shortage.The developments come as both sides continue to suffer casualties and infrastructure losses, while Moscow seeks additional manpower for its more than four-year-old invasion of Ukraine.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russians are still fleeing abroad, citing fears of a new mobilization and a loss of freedom
articles.summary: This summer, a 28-year-old digital content marketer packed up his suitcases and duct-taped boxes and fled Russia, leaving behind his family and friends and n...
articles.body:
This summer, a 28-year-old digital content marketer packed up his suitcases and duct-taped boxes and fled Russia, leaving behind his family and friends and not knowing when he'll be able to return.

"It is very sad to leave Russia," he said in the southern city of Krasnodar before heading for the border with Georgia.

He blamed "the political situation" in Russia and complications over authorities restricting internet access as his reasons for leaving. Otherwise, "I never would have left for more than several months," he told The Associated Press, speaking on condition of anonymity because of security concerns.

He is one of a number of people who either left or are contemplating a move amid recent Ukrainian drone attacks inside Russia and persistent rumors of a coming mobilization of troops for the 4 1/2-year-old war.

The attacks this summer caused an unprecedented fuel crisis and dealt crippling blows to the booming e-commerce sector . Since last year, the government has cited the attacks to justify harsh restrictions on connecting to the internet.

The exodus is nowhere near as large as in 2022, when hundreds of thousands fled in the first year of the full-scale invasion. Still, a group that helps citizens who flee abroad said it received nearly eight times more queries last month than it had in May.

"It doesn't mean that there is a huge number of people right now at the borders," said Anastasia Burakova, the founder of Kovcheg, which means "ark" in Russian. "But we're seeing that people are preparing to emigrate, we're seeing that people are looking into what options are there."

On social media, Russians talk of moving abroad

The current numbers are hard to gauge. Unlike 2022, when droves of men fled a partial call-up for the military, there are no lines at border crossings or shortages of plane tickets to visa-free destinations like Armenia, Georgia, Kazakhstan and Turkey at the moment.

At the same time, AP found numerous social media videos from all over Russia of people saying they had decided to leave, citing war-related reasons. Others were worried about the declining economy , an uncertain future and shrinking freedoms.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other officials in Kyiv have said Russia is planning another mobilization after the State Duma election that concludes Sunday — claims the Kremlin has repeatedly and vehemently rejected.

Yan Slovitsky, an urgent assistance coordinator for Kovcheg, described "a panicked wave" of emigration since mid-July linked to mobilization fears, the fuel crisis and internet restrictions.

A Moscow-based diplomat told AP about "a palpable rise in public anxiety this summer," and pointed to "anecdotal evidence of higher than usual numbers of Russians appearing in neighboring Georgia and Armenia, possibly fearing another mobilization after the Duma elections." The diplomat was not authorized to comment publicly and thus spoke on condition of anonymity.

Alen Simonyan, secretary of Armenia's Security Council, told independent Russian TV channel Dozhd last month that his country "will not interfere in any way, and if necessary, will help" Russians who are moving there to avoid being drafted.

That drew a sharp rebuke from the Russian Foreign Ministry, which called Simonyan's remark "provocative."

Russian lawmaker Viktor Sobolev told the RTVI channel that the country doesn't need people who "don't love their Motherland so much that they leave because of rumors," adding: "Let them leave."

Some emigres seek to avoid military service

The digital content marketer, who describes himself as a pacifist, says this was his second attempt at emigrating.

He left Russia in 2022 to avoid the partial call-up of 300,000 new troops, an announcement by President Vladimir Putin that shocked the nation.

He said he isn't technically eligible for military service in peacetime due to a hip ailment, but felt it was safer to leave because he didn't know what to expect from authorities.

Some officials in 2022 said such men could legally be drafted in a mobilization, as did some rights groups helping conscripts. Others said martial law had to be declared for it to be legal. Russia has not formally declared war on Ukraine, and the Kremlin only imposed martial law in the four Ukrainian regions it illegally annexed in 2022 but doesn't fully control.

The digital content marketer returned to his hometown of Ulyanovsk in 2025 and worked remotely for clients in other countries. But Russia's unrelenting clampdown on thousands of internet platforms, sites and services made it harder for him to do his job, he said, having to switch virtual private network servers to find one allowing him to get around the restrictions.

Another factor was the rumored new mobilization. "You never know what will happen tomorrow," he said from an apartment in the Georgian capital of Tbilisi, where he settled.

A 23-year-old Muscovite who left Russia last month also cited the persistent mobilization rumors and fears that her husband might end up in the military.

The woman, who spoke to AP on condition of anonymity because of security concerns, said her father narrowly escaped being drafted in 2022 by fleeing the country. This year, her husband learned he would no longer have a deferment from military service after getting his master's degree.

"A person can figure anything out, but we were really afraid that (my husband) could end up in the army, because at this point it is a one-way ticket," she said.

Ivan Nazarov, a new university graduate who moved to the Armenian capital of Yerevan, echoed her sentiment.

He said he was aware of reports of conscripts in mandatory service who are not supposed to be deployed to Ukraine being forced to sign contracts that send them to the battlefield.

"For me, it is a question of survival," Nazarov added, speaking at a gathering organized by Kovcheg in Yerevan for new immigrants.

Queer activist Daniil Neonov left Russia this summer after a series of detentions and a 10-day jail term on charges of displaying extremist symbols — a photo featuring a T-shirt with a rainbow-colored print on it he posted on social media.

Russian authorities have outlawed what they call "the international LGBT movement" as extremist, leading sometimes to misdemeanor charges for carrying items with a rainbow on them.

Neonov told AP in Yerevan that he feared a criminal case would be brought against him.

He said he knows other people who left Russia after being detained for gathering outside the Supreme Court last month to support the opposition Yabloko party when the court struck it from the parliamentary election ballot . Yabloko was the only party on the ballot that openly opposed the war.

"The police came to them and filed reports. I know several people who, after they were held in detention, also left. I mean, I'm not the only one," Neonov said.

A 35-year-old Russian told AP he was preparing for leaving the country because he doesn't want to live in a land without free speech, where the economy is on a downward spiral and where schoolchildren have to listen to propaganda touting war, normalizing violence and promoting isolation from the rest of the world.

The man, who also spoke on condition of anonymity for safety reasons, said he had been thinking about leaving Russia for over a decade but still had hope that "everything would work out."

Now, he said, Russians "live in a huge digital jail. You can't say anything, you can't do anything. You have absolutely no rights."

Sophiko Megrelidze in Tbilisi, Georgia, and Ani Khachatryan in Yerevan, Armenia, contributed.

articles.title: Peers to debate donations law changes after Reform's £72m windfall
articles.summary: The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats.
articles.body:
The House of Lords will debate changes to the laws on political donations later on Monday after Reform UK received £72m from two billionaires in 24 hours.

Calls for restrictions are growing after huge donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a £100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

The leader of one of Labour's biggest funders, Unite the Union, is among those backing limits on individual donations. In response, Nigel Farage's party has accused Labour of trying to "rig the system".

The sheer scale of Reform's record-breaking donation windfall has prompted an urgent debate across the parties.

On Monday, the bill that would introduce a £100,000 cap on donations from British voters living abroad returns to the House of Lords.

The rules were proposed in a review by former civil servant Philip Rycroft aimed at countering foreign influence in UK politics.

The Labour peer Lord Wills told Radio 4's Westminster Hour he intended to amend the bill so that donations from those living in the UK could also be capped.

Sharon Graham, the general secretary of Unite, told the BBC a limit on individual donations was necessary.

Her union has donated large sums to Labour in recent years, but she argues that "billionaires splashing out millions" is different from "everyday workers giving 10p a week to a political fund".

Reform have said "Labour and their union pals know they can't win an election fairly so now they want to rig the system".

Questions remain over whether Reform will be able to keep all of the £72m.

Robert Jenrick, the party's economic spokesman, told the BBC on Sunday the donations were "entirely in line with the law as it is, and as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future".

The government has also proposed a minimum residency period in which the £100,000 cap would still apply for those who move back to the UK.

This would be in place for the rest of the calendar year and the following calendar year after the person returns.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the rule changes would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".

Rayner added she was not commenting specifically on Delo and Harborne as she did not "understand" their "circumstances".

The Times reported in June that Harborne, who has been based in Thailand, had registered to vote in the UK, while Delo had told the Telegraph in April that he was moving back from Hong Kong.

BBC News has been told both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

The government has previously said it was "determined to tackle" the issue of "mega-donors", and has established a new taskforce to do this.

articles.title: 'A ceremony of light': First-ever Ganga Aarti held on River Thames in London - video
articles.summary: UK News: Thousands of people gathered on the banks of the River Thames on Sunday for the first-ever Ganga Aarti in London, a traditional Hindu ceremony of ligh.
articles.body: Thousands of people gathered on the banks of the River Thames on Sunday for the first-ever Ganga Aarti in London, a traditional Hindu ceremony of light and thanksgiving.Titled “Ganga Aarti on the Thames: A Ceremony of Light”, the event was organised by Chinmaya Mission UK in collaboration with the annual Totally Thames festival. It was part of global celebrations marking the 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission.The ceremony recreated the spirit of the world-famous Ganga Aarti held along the River Ganges in India. Organisers described it as a symbol of the life-giving flow of nature, knowledge and consciousness.“For generations, communities have gathered on the banks of Ganga to offer light in gratitude for the river, for nature and for all that sustains life,” said Brahmacharini Shripriya Chaitanya, resident teacher of Chinmaya Mission UK, according to PTI.“Ganga Aarti on the Thames carries that same spirit, bringing people together in a shared moment of gratitude, hope and unity,” she added.The traditional ceremony involved large, multi-tiered oil lamps, prayers, music and chanting. It was held against the backdrop of the historic Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich and brought together spiritual leaders, representatives of Hindu organisations and members of South Asian communities from across the UK.Chaitanya said the River Ganges also symbolised the flow of knowledge for Chinmaya Mission. “Our founder, Swami Chinmayananda, dedicated his life to bringing the timeless wisdom of Vedanta -- one of the great philosophical traditions of Hinduism, from the Himalayas into people's everyday lives. As we mark 75 years of Chinmaya Mission, this event is also a celebration of that legacy: of knowledge, service and gratitude flowing beyond boundaries,” she said, PTI reported.The ceremony took place entirely on land, with no material from the event placed, poured or released into the River Thames.Chinmaya Mission UK said the event was intended as a celebration for the British Hindu and wider South Asian communities, while also inviting people of all backgrounds to reflect on gratitude and respect for nature.“At its heart, Ganga Aarti reminds us not to take the natural world for granted. Gratitude towards nature should be expressed not only through prayer, but through the care and responsibility with which we treat the environment around us,” the organisation said.Chinmaya Mission, founded in 1951, is a global movement focused on spiritual education, inner transformation and the teachings of Vedanta. It has more than 350 centres worldwide and runs cultural, educational and service initiatives. The first Ganga Aarti event, which was sold out, is expected to pave the way for it to become a more regular annual feature of the festival.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
